correctness.rationale: For any putative scalar-shifted monomial the valuation and initial coefficient are forced; normalizing leaves a unit. Removing (1-y^j) factors successively determines unique exponents mod 19 through degree 18. Frobenius gives (1-y^j)^19 = 1 mod y^19, so this test applies to arbitrary integer powers, including negative powers. P0 is trivial in this truncation and each Pa forces equal exponents at a and 19-a. An independent reproduction computes integral colored-partition coefficients through q^379 via n p9(n) = 9 sum_{j=1}^n sigma_1(j) p9(n-j), then reduces mod 19 and removes Euler factors by geometric-series division. It reproduces every row, with valuation 1 only at residues 6 and 13; the pair (1,18) disagrees except at residue 3, where (2,17) gives (10,18). The finite mismatch contradicts any full identity; infinite vanishing at 17 instead follows from Bilgici's dissection, not the computed zero truncation.
residual_risks: The certificate tests only the specified multiplicative alphabet; it does not decide identities using other theta factors.
